### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via HookContextSchema (symbol, a top-level const), ScriptContext (symbol, a top-level interface))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via HookContextSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7b3d5585ca9deab5c627eaa826a6d622a1a8cd68` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cd7647da48c202eada0c5be6b6856563baceaf86` — the merge of head `7e4509b6cb666ad6fa8fa5b26a063ee7ae15886f` into base `7b3d5585ca9deab5c627eaa826a6d622a1a8cd68`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cd7647da48c202eada0c5be6b6856563baceaf86 && git checkout cd7647da48c202eada0c5be6b6856563baceaf86
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7b3d5585ca9deab5c627eaa826a6d622a1a8cd68 7e4509b6cb666ad6fa8fa5b26a063ee7ae15886f && git checkout -B drift-repro 7b3d5585ca9deab5c627eaa826a6d622a1a8cd68 && git merge --no-ff 7e4509b6cb666ad6fa8fa5b26a063ee7ae15886f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7b3d5585ca9deab5c627eaa826a6d622a1a8cd68
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7b3d5585ca9deab5c627eaa826a6d622a1a8cd68` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

`domain:spec` seat 4 (#18917) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_0121ooBYRmS8ziFXm9ai5YHm` · claim `6164006610` on #23221 · reviewed head `7e4509b6cb666ad6fa8fa5b26a063ee7ae15886f` · 2026-10-14T11:17Z

**Verdict: ACCEPT.** Not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 23458`: 0 of 11 paths), 11 files, +672 / −1. It lands after the landing clauses in item 6.

1. **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #23221`, `Clause-②: yes` at line start in the body and the changeset (`minor` for spec, objectql and runtime). No other closing keyword sits beside a card number. `mergeable_state` clean.
2. **Premises against the dispatch's ruling.**
   - The seat's naming ruling and its premise held: `referentialCascadeDelete` had 0 hits repo-wide, against 7 for the control `referentialFieldClear`.
   - The key is declared beside `referentialFieldClear` in `hook.zod.ts`. It is optional, the engine writes `true` or omits it, and its docblock is the contract text: meaning, absence, why it is declared, trust model.
   - Ruling #1165 (no undeclared-key sniffing) holds by construction: no `__`-prefixed spelling exists. The engine marks the cascade's child delete through an engine-private `AsyncLocalStorage` record keyed on that child's object and id, claimed once by `delete()` before middleware and hooks, and projected onto the declared key in both phases.
   - The QuickJS carrier is `buildSandboxContext`, `installCtx` and the `ScriptContext` type.
   - The changeset's guard idiom reads only declared keys (`ctx.previous` is declared at `hook.zod.ts:798` on `main`).
3. **Gates and evidence, pinned to this head.** Check-runs on `7e4509b6c`: 36 success, 5 skipped, 0 failures. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (1–6/6), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset` and `Spec property liveness` all succeeded. Pins cover the four faces triage named: the child sees the key; a hand delete of the same child does not; a `set_null` cleanup keeps `referentialFieldClear` without this key; a sandboxed body reads it. Further pins cover grandchildren, and a hook-issued `ctx.api` delete is not marked. The ablations went red exactly on their pins (A1–A4). A5, the object and id key check, stayed green as predicted: it is a defensive invariant with no reachable counter-case.
4. **Accepted deviations.**
   - PM mechanism assumption 1 was measured and replaced: a `__` stamp on the child context would ride into deletes a child's hooks issue through `ctx.api`. Its replacement meets the ruling more strictly.
   - The gate list grew from 77 to 115 on the final diff, and all 115 ran.
   - One `origin/main` merge was made through `os-regen-merge.sh` before the PR opened.
   - The shared clone was deepened as two shallow-refusing gates prescribed.
5. **Out-of-scope dispositions.** One wording-precision observation, `carrier:` none, noted and not filed: the `cascadeDeleteSets` docblock's "absent context turns present" holds only on the `none` and `split` plans. The new docblock states the narrower form.
6. **Landing clauses.**
   - (a) A `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` `## Contract review` PASS on the landing head: published schema face (`packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`) plus the `Clause-②: yes` declaration.
   - (b) Every check green on the landing head.
   - (c) `mergeable_state` clean at enqueue.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7e4509b6cb666ad6fa8fa5b26a063ee7ae15886f`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Gate verdicts are the head's check-runs: 41 on `7e4509b6cb666ad6fa8fa5b26a063ee7ae15886f`, 36 success, 5 skipped (Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood matrix shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance — each path- or opt-in-filtered), 0 failures. Governed Surface Queue Guard success; the file list (11 paths) touches no governed surface. Face: a published schema (`packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts`), hence this tier.

- **The new `HookContext` key — right.** `HookContextSchema.referentialCascadeDelete` is `z.boolean().optional()` beside `referentialFieldClear`, on a schema the file header keeps deliberately non-strict, so the engine-written key survives `.parse()` and an absent key stays absent (never `false`, never present-but-undefined). Accept-set change: a widening of the published `HookContext` type (z.input of the schema); nothing previously valid changes meaning. The docblock is the contract text and declares the two consequences of the no-envelope design (a hook's own `ctx.api` writes are not marked; nothing the child delete is handed moves). Pinned in `hook.test.ts`: survives a parse typed, absent when not carried, a key of its own against the twin.
- **The engine's marking rule — right.** The walk opens one engine-private `cascadeIssuedDeletes` AsyncLocalStorage token per `cascade` dependent, around only its own `this.delete(childName, { where: { id: depId }, context })`; `delete()` claims it once at engine.ts 18884, after `resolveEngineDeleteDispatch` (a scalar `where.id` resolves to `by-id`, so `id` is bound) and before `opCtx`, middleware and hooks. The `opensAfterAbortUnit` re-entry at 18840 to 18842 returns before the claim, so the inner call that dispatches the hooks is the claimant. The projection is a conditional spread on the one hook-context object `afterDelete` reuses, so both phases carry it. The context still reaches the child by reference, unchanged.
- **Its exclusions — right, each pinned in `engine-cascade-delete.test.ts`.** Root delete and a hand delete of the same child under the same identity: no token, absent. Bulk or `multi` deletes: `id` undefined, never a cascade shape. The `set_null` cleanup: an update, keeps `referentialFieldClear` only (engine.ts 16279) and never this key; a cascade child delete never carries the update twin. Writes a cascaded child's hooks issue through `ctx.api`: the same token is already claimed, so `issued.claimed` short-circuits, and a different row also fails the object/id match. Grandchildren: the child's own walk opens its own token, marked at any depth. An identity-less cascade is marked and the envelope carries no `__` key.
- **Trust model — right.** The hook context is assembled member by member (`session`, `provenance`, `user`, `api`, `transaction`) with no spread of `opCtx.context`, so a client-supplied `referentialCascadeDelete` on a request context never reaches `ctx`; the fact has no operation-private spelling, so there is nothing on `ctx.api`, `ctx.transaction` or a `__` key to sniff — the ruling on objectstack-ai/hotcrm#1165 holds by construction. The key is a signal, not an authorization input; plugin-security reads nothing new.
- **Declared divergence from the update twin — right.** The twin's docblock gives hook-issued writes envelope semantics (they inherit the `__` marker); this key gives dispatch semantics (a hook's own delete is not cascade-issued). That is the card's letter — true exactly on each child delete the cascade issues, absent on every other delete — and the docblock states the divergence as contract rather than leaving it implicit.
- **The sandbox carrier — right.** `buildSandboxContext` spreads `{ referentialCascadeDelete: true }` only on `=== true`; `installCtx` does `vm.setProp(ctxObj, 'referentialCascadeDelete', vm.true)` under the same guard; `ScriptContext` gains the optional member with its docblock. These are the twin's three sites exactly. `QuickJSScriptRunner` is the only `ScriptRunner` implementation besides `UnimplementedScriptRunner`, so no second carrier is missing. The cli `lowered-body-face-enumeration` pin classifies conditional spreads on both faces, so the key appears on both and introduces no in-process-only member. Pinned from inside the VM (`referential-cascade-delete-signal.integration.test.ts`: real ObjectQL, SqlDriver, QuickJS runner; both phases true with the inherited `session.userId`; the hand delete of a sibling line under the same identity reads `typeof` as `'undefined'`; the update twin absent on both).
- **Regenerated authorable surface and reference doc — right.** `packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json` gains `data/HookContext:referentialCascadeDelete` in sorted position; `content/docs/references/data/hook.mdx` (auto-generated header) gains the row built from the `.describe()` text, in source order after the twin. Both are byte-exact per the green `TypeScript Type Check` job, which runs every spec generated-artifact gate. `authorable-surface.base.json` is untouched — right, it is the `baseRev` anchor written only by `gen:schema` from a git-resolved baseline. `api-surface/data.json` and `json-schema.manifest/data.json` record exports and schema names, not members (neither lists the twin), so no further regeneration is owed. No liveness row is owed: `HookContextSchema` is not a registered metadata type, the twin has none, and `Spec property liveness` is success.
- **ADR coverage — right as stated.** `docs/adr` at the head names neither `referentialFieldClear`, `cascadeDeleteRelations` nor `walkReferencingRelations`; ADR-0025 and ADR-0102 govern sandbox tiers and CPU budget, not the ctx member set; ADR-0058 D2 governs the `input.options` projection, untouched. The engine.ts anchor (ADR-0057, ADR-0067, ADR-0119 transaction seam) is a region the diff does not touch; the anchor gate is inside the green lint job.
- **Card pins, all four present:** cascade child `beforeDelete` sees the key; hand delete of the same child does not; set-null cleanup keeps `referentialFieldClear` and not this key; the sandboxed body reads it.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/23221-cascade-delete-hook-signal.md`: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime` at `minor` — matches what the diff publishes: a widening of a published schema, the engine assembly that populates it, and the sandbox members that carry it. All three are public (no `private` flag), members of the `fixed` group, pre-mode tag `next`, so the group moves to the next `next.N` together. Nothing removed or renamed; no migration and no ADR-0087 disposition owed. `Check Changeset` is success.
- `Clause-②: yes` — right: declared in the PR body and repeated in the changeset body, with no arm, which the rule allows (at most one; a widening needs none); `yes` takes at least `minor`, and `minor` is what is declared.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none in the `os-dev-report`. Every dev flag answered; nothing escalated.

- **Mechanism deviation (ALS token instead of a `__` stamp on the child context) — accepted as right.** Both stated reasons hold at the head: `api: this.buildHookApi(opCtx.context)` hands the delete's own context to the scoped repositories, so a stamp would ride into every hook-issued write; and a stamp needs a fresh object, turning an absent caller context into a present one, the very reason the `cascadeDeleteSets` docblock already rejects a context key. The dispatch's mechanism assumption is not an input to this review.
- **Gate list 77 to 115 — accepted.** Derived from the final diff; the head's check-runs are the verdict in any case.
- **One merge of `origin/main` before opening, none after — accepted.** The head contains merge commit `92980cc027`; `mergeable_state` is clean.
- **Deepened the shared clone, advancing shared `refs/remotes/origin/main` — noted, no action.** A hazard flagged for siblings, as the discipline asks; not a breach.
- **Stopped its own runner processes by recorded PID — accepted.** Within the rule: never a process it did not start.
- **`engine.ts` additions beyond the claim's line anchors (`CascadeIssuedDelete`, `cascadeIssuedDeletes`) — accepted.** Both are the cascade dispatch machinery the claim's file surface names; disjoint from PR #23412's regions, which has landed and is merged into this head.
- **Attribution — right.** All six branch commits end with the session-URL trailer plus the model-free co-author line AGENTS.md prescribes; the PR body footer is the session-URL form; no model identifier appears in the diff, the changeset or the PR body.
- **Out-of-scope finding (`cascadeDeleteSets` docblock says a context key would make an absent context present "on every nested delete", imprecise under the atomic plan) — not filing is right.** A wording imprecision in an untouched docblock is neither a reproducible defect, a contract violation nor an authoring trap (Prime Directive 10); it is recorded in the report's `out_of_scope_findings`, and the new `cascadeIssuedDeletes` docblock states the narrower form. No action owed before landing.
- **Acceptance note A5 (the object/id key check has no reachable counter-case) — accepted.** The claim precedes middleware and hooks, so nothing enters `delete()` inside an unclaimed token first; keeping the check as a defensive invariant without a pin is right, since a pin would need a path that does not exist. Claim-once (A4) is the pinned half.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23221-cascade-delete-hook-signal`
Reviewed-by: `session_0121ooBYRmS8ziFXm9ai5YHm`

**VERDICT: PASS**
